A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 17-page MoLingo paper, including the complete five-page supplement. Text and rendered content match apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its placement.

before.justification: v2 reports original motion-generation results, ablations, a user study, and humanoid-controller demonstrations, including supplementary experiments in Tables 5–9.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, user-study outcomes, and humanoid-controller demonstrations reported in v2, including the supplementary results.

M1.justification: The semantically aligned autoencoder, repetitive-token filtering, multi-token cross-attention, masked autoregressive rectified-flow generation, losses, and inference procedure are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HumanML3D coverage, BABEL frame-level annotations, HumanML3D-272 representation, and humanoid motion-transfer scenario. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1, 8, and 9 and in the qualitative comparisons. The user study retains MoMask, DisCoRD, and MotionStreamer as its three comparators.

E3.justification: The MARDM-67, MS-272, and TMR-263 evaluation protocols are unchanged, as are preprocessing, training budgets, model configurations, metrics, sampling settings, and user-study procedures.

E4.justification: The same analyses cover text conditioning, autoencoder variants, semantic-loss choices, latent size, adapter depth, token filtering, and inference steps. Tables 2–3 and 5–7 and the qualitative demonstrations contain no revised analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 20-run evaluation and 95% confidence intervals in Tables 1, 8, and 9. Repeated-run descriptions and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match, including supplementary results. For example, Table 1 retains VAE FID 0.049 and SAE Top-1 R-Precision 0.544; Table 8 retains MoLingo FID 3.415.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, mathematical definitions, the notation table, and supplementary temporal-window reasoning are identical. No assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about semantic alignment, multi-token cross-attention, and state-of-the-art motion generation. Contribution scope and claimed novelty are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of semantic regularization, conditioning, latent size, and motion quality are unchanged. Both versions retain the same limitation concerning detailed hand movements.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1 and 6 and Table 10 retain identical architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, training-time, and sampling details. The project link and promise to release code and models are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and all 88 reference entries are identical. No cited work or substantive relationship to prior research changes.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 26 Mar 2026 to v3 dated 13 Jul 2026. The title, authors, prose, headings, and document structure, including the supplement, are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp is repositioned. Figures 1–7, Tables 1–10, and the paper's content layout are unchanged; pages 2–17 render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves v2's scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information, including the complete supplement. Updating and repositioning the arXiv stamp has no meaningful effect on the paper's overall quality.
